mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% in the month preceding the prediction is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to reduced risk-free discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when FEDFUNDS > 5.25%, or inflation proxies (CPIAUCSL) show no acceleration.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment months) exceeding 1,000 above the prior month's level coincides with a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as labor market expansion supports corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative despite consistent monthly employment growth above the threshold, or other demand proxies (GDPC1, HOUST) show no correlation.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising HOUST (residential construction) by at least 10% relative to the prior month predict a positive S&P 20-day forward return as it signals renewed consumer and business confidence.
candidate_trigger: HOUST grows by at least 10% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive when HOUST growth meets the trigger, or other demand indicators (GDPC1, RSAFS) contradict the pattern.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) of 5% or more for three consecutive months predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return as it reflects weakening manufacturing momentum and reduced earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by at least 5% monthly for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite the supply shock, or INDPRO recovers before the prediction window.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 1% for two consecutive months in a low-inflation regime (CPIAUCSL < 237), the S&P 60-day forward return is predicted to be positive due to lower real interest rates and increased equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 237 AND FEDFUNDS < 1% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both triggers are met, or FEDFUNDS unexpectedly rises.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in UNRATE (unemployment rate) below 4% triggers a positive S&P 20-day forward return as lower labor market friction supports corporate cost structures and investor optimism.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite UNRATE crossing below 4%, or other labor indicators (PAYEMS) contradict the signal.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in GDPC1 (GDP demand) and RSAFS (retail sales) of at least 2% each over the prior month predict a positive S&P 5-day forward return as dual demand signals reinforce optimism.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > GDPC1 previous month * 1.02 AND RSAFS > RSAFS previous month * 1.02
failure_condition: 5-day forward return is not positive despite both triggers, or the correlation between proxies is weak (<0.6).

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a contractionary industrial policy regime (indicated by a sharp drop in INDPRO and a sustained rise in UNRATE above 5%) predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return as investor fears of supply-side shocks increase.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by 8% month-over-month AND UNRATE > 5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative when both triggers are met, or other supply indicators (HOUST) show no decline.
